fixes.explanation: Good thought, but no. I'm a sucker for a nice mantle, and I own exactly one apron. Isaiah is the one delivering this promise, but he doesn't point at himself: "Your eyes will see the King in His beauty…" The sight is the King, with a land that stretches afar too.

Elders is a decent guess, and I'd have said it with full confidence too, which is how I end up wrong a lot. But the verse names someone else: "…even the lame will carry off plunder." I bet the lame are the last ones you'd picture hauling off loot. The spoils are so abundant that even they carry some away.

Strangers didn't make the guest list on this one, baker. Isaiah says, "…even the lame will carry off plunder." I think the surprise is who's carrying it, since the lame aren't who you'd expect to haul off loot. With an abundance of spoils divided, even they walk away with plunder.

Written down sounds like a ledger, baker, and I spent years in a drawer full of old receipts. A ledger holds on to every entry, though, and that's not what the verse says. Isaiah says, "The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity." The iniquity is forgiven, and that's the last line of the chapter.

problems.problem: The mantle and apron aside does not explain the choice; the rest mainly repeats that Isaiah names the King.
The self-deprecating aside adds personality, but the explanation still mainly repeats who is named in the verse.
The guest-list line adds a comparison, but the explanation still mainly repeats who is named in the verse.
